business_problem: Amway needed secure, scalable AI infrastructure that could support assistants across internal operations and seller-facing workflows while improving inference efficiency, reducing rollout times, and preventing sensitive data leakage.
solution_summary: Amway standardized its internal AI rollout on NVIDIA AI Enterprise to support assistants for employees and Amway Business Owners without sacrificing governance or performance. The company uses NVIDIA NIM to accelerate inference for its office assistant and AM Copilot experiences, and it embeds NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails across the workflow to screen prompts and responses for sensitive information. For lifecycle management, Amway runs NVIDIA Base Command Manager Essentials to automate model training, deployment, monitoring, and GPU resource operations across the stack. The assistants connect document-processing and knowledge-base tasks with business logic so marketers and support staff can retrieve cases, generate presentations, and deliver personalized guidance at scale. This architecture let Amway move secure generative AI use cases from experiments into on-premises production with better throughput, faster rollout cycles, and tighter compliance controls.

data_flow: Documents, knowledge-base content, and business logic are routed into on-premises assistants running on AI Enterprise. NIM serves the inference layer for office and seller-facing copilots, Guardrails filters inputs and outputs for sensitive content, and Base Command Manager Essentials orchestrates training, deployment, and monitoring across the environment.
integration_points: On-premises employee and marketer assistant workflows
business_outcome: Amway improved inference efficiency by 40 percent, blocked 99.9 percent of sensitive information, shortened a major delivery cycle from 35 days to 15 days, improved operational efficiency by more than 60 percent, and put assistants into production for office work and marketer support.
